findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a food handler on staff who had not signed their Employee Health Reporting Agreement. CORRECTED- employee read and signed the SCDPH acknowledgement of reportable food-borne illnesses. Ensure all food handlers are aware of reportable Foodborne illnesses, and symptoms associated with food borne illness.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Allergen awareness notice
findings.comment:
Inspector observed no Allergen awareness signage posted. Inspector will either email or drop off a paper copy to the person in charge (PIC) so that the allergen notice may be posted to be visible at the point of sale. Facilities should display an allergen notice to remind consumers to report potential food associated allergens to the facility.

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple employees don gloves without washing hands first. CORRECTED- education about times to wash hands was reviewed with staff. All employees should wash hands prior to donning gloves to engage in food handling, and after engaging in any activity which may contaminate hands to prevent the contamination of foods.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the serving line hand washing sink being used as a dump sink when preparing a new sanitizer buckets (see violation #16). CORRECTED- education was conducted about the usage of hand washing sinks. Ensure all sinks designated for hand washing are used for hand washing ONLY- so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.[Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed with no measurable chlorine concentration after 3 runs of the dish machine. The person in charge (PIC) called their service provider and prepared the triple sink for sanitation in the meantime. CORRECTED- The dish machine was observed to dispense 100 ppm Chlorine after the service provider replaced the sanitizer. Ensure staff knows how to change chemical sanitizer. Test the dish machine at least once daily to ensure proper sanitation of food contact surfaces. Due to the history of this dish machine failing to meet sanitation concentrations/ temperatures, inspector highly recommends keeping a log of daily sanitizer concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).  [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The quaternary ammonia sanitizer buckets along the line (used for food contact surfaces) were observed to be at a low concentration. CORRECTED- sanitizer buckets were remade to 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are remade and tested at a frequency to hold the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonia, 50-200 ppm for Chlorine- the active ingredient in bleach).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the only (2) tubes of quaternary ammonia test strips within the facility to be expired. The facility uses quaternary ammonia for chemical sanitation of food contact surfaces within the triple sink and sanitizer buckets. CORRECTED- the chemical service provider who serviced the dish machine (see violation #16) gave the facility in-date test strips. Ensure chemicals used for sanitation of food contact surfaces have an in-date test kit to verify proper concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
One employee was observed to have an expired food handler certificate, and multiple other employees on staff during today’s inspection did not have Food Handler Certificates. All employees who participate in any degree of food handling must obtain a Food Handlers Certificate within 30 days of hire, to be maintained every 3 years. The Inspector provided a list of ANSI-approved food handler courses to the PIC. Ensure all staff who have not completed a Certified Food Protection Manager’s course obtain Food Handlers by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Coleslaw stored on prep table in ice bath was observed at 55F (probed). The ice in the ice bath had melted, and was no longer sufficient. PIC was informed of out-of-temperature coleslaw and the item was discarded and replaced. The ice in the bath was replenished as well. Ensure that the ice bath is monitored with enough frequency to ensure the coleslaw is held at a temperature of 41F or lower at all times. Time as a control may be used as an alternative. Using time as a control, coleslaw could be kept on the counter at any temperature as long as it is used or discarded within 4 hours. A form will need to be completed with the Sangamon County Department of Public Health to enact time as a control for this item.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
Brownies stored by the cash register were observed without any labeling. Informed PIC that all foods packaged in the establishment need to be clearly labeled with the common name of the food, name of the establishment, and the ingredients of the product (preferably in descending order by weight). Ensure employees are placing labels on the brownies before presenting them to the public. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Conveyor belt dish machine observed to have an inconsistent final rinse temperature on a plate surface after four - six runs through the machine. The temperature was checked using inspector’s dish thermometer, facility’s dish thermometer, and a recently calibrated probe thermometer. The gauge at rinse is inconsistent and showing 170 to 180 on the dial. Staff will use the dish machine to wash and rinse and then the triple compartment sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is fixed. Make necessary repairs to the dish machine so it is reaching a final rinse temperature of 160F on the plate thermometer. Monitor the dish machine’s rinse temperature to ensure it is reaching an effective sanitizing temperature. Dish thermometers were reading anywhere from 145F to 164F.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. [P]

4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. findings.comment:
Three dented cans removed from the dry storage area to be discarded or returned to the supplier. CORRECTED- Discussed dented cans and their potential for botulism. Monitor cans as they are being stocked, and return or discard any dented cans. If a can is dented in the facility, it may be opened and used immediately.
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs observed stored above iceberg lettuce in the walk-in cooler. PIC stated that the eggs belong to an employee. CORRECTED- Eggs were moved to proper storage. Discussed storage order, and storage of employees personal foods.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Conveyor belt dish machine observed to have a final rinse temperature of 154F on a plate surface after four runs through the machine. Staff can use the 3 compartment sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is fixed. Make necessary repairs to the dish machien so it is reaching a final rinse temperature of 165F on the plate thermometer, or 180F on the built-in thermometer.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Quat sanitizer from the 3 compartment sink wall-mounted dispenser observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- PIC adjusted the machine and concentrated sanitizer jug. Sanitizer was then observed at 400ppm quat. Discussed monitoring sanitizer concentration using test strips.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on the label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Coleslaw at the make line observed at 57F (probed). The pan was held using ice as the only means of temperature control. Discussed using time as a control and created a policy. Employees will note the time the coleslaw is removed from cold holding and placed on the countertop. Coleslaw will be used or discarded within 4 hours of being removed from cold holding.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
The final rinse temperature dial on the dish machine was observed holding steady at 120F (and never moving), despite the inspector’s dish plate thermometer reading at 154F. Repair the built-in dish machine thermometer so it accurately reflects the water temperature.
4-204.115: A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Caulking along the dish machine drainboards is observed to be molding and separating from the wall. Clean and reseal the dish machine drainboards to the wall.
2) Caulking sealing the splash guards to the back handwashing sink has deteriorated. Clean and reseal the splash guards to the back handwashing sink.
3) Water was observed ponding near the entrance near the dish area and in the corner under the 3 compartment sink. Make necessary changes or repairs to prevent and minimize water ponding.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Facility does not have proof of food handler training for any employees, except for one observed on file. Ensure all food employees complete food handler training. Keep certificates on file.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: PIC has not completed allergen training. Ensure all CFMs complete ANSI-approved allergen training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
REPEAT: No employee reporting agreements on file. Inspector emailed facility an employee reporting agreement. Print copies review with employees, and have them sign agreements. Ensure all food employees have signed reporting agreements on file.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Conveyor belt dish machine observed to have a final rinse temperature of 155F on a plate surface on the first run, then approx. 145 on subsequent runs through. CORRECTED- PICs adjusted hot water settings and were able to reach a rinse temp of 175F. Dish machine provider was contacted for service to ensure machine is functioning properly. Ensure dish machine is reaching a final rinse temperature of 165F on the disk thermometer, or 180F on the built-in thermometer.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Open gallon of milk observed without date marking. CORRECTED- PIC labeled milk with the date it was opened. Discussed date marking requirements- ensure milk is labeled with the date opened and used or discarded within 7 days of opening.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Two spray bottles containing blue liquid observed unlabeled. CORRECTED- PIC labeled bottles to indicate their contents (glass cleaner).
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Container of employee food observed stored in the cooler under the front service counter. Ensure employee personal items/foods are stored in a designated area below/away from foods intended for service. 
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Facility does not have proof of food handler training for any employees, except for the CFM and one other. Ensure all food employees complete food handler training. Keep certificates on file.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
PIC has not completed allergen training. Ensure all CFMs complete ANSI-approved allergen training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
No employee reporting agreements on file. CORRECTED- Inspector emailed facility an employee reporting agreement. PIC printed copies and had employees present review and sign agreements. Ensure all food employees have signed reporting agreements on file.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
No vomit/diarrhea clean up kit or policy available. CORRECTED- Inspector emailed a norovirus clean up policy to PIC. Print policy and keep on hand in case of vomit/diarrhea events in the facility.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Employee observed to wash hands, then use clean hands to turn faucet off without the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed handwashing procedure with employee, who rewashed hands. Review handwashing procedure with all employees. Ensure a barrier (ex. paper towel) is used to prevent recontamination of hands.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Conveyor belt dish machine observed to have a final rinse temperature of 120F on a plate surface after running three loads through. After several more, rinse temperature reached 140F, but began to fall again on the following load. Dish machine provider was contacted for service. Use the three-compartment sink until dish machine is reaching a final rinse temperature of 165F on the disk thermometer, or 180F on the built-in thermometer.
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Metal container containing portions of ranch dressing observed with a date label of 8-23. CORRECTED- Per discussion with PIC, ranch dressing was portioned yesterday. Container was relabeled to indicate such. Clean old date labels off of containers and ensure foods are labeled with the date prepared/opened.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Soil accumulation, several lids, and other debris observed under and to the right of the kitchen ice machine. Clean around ice machine.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Caulking around the mop sink is starting to separate off the wall. See that caulking is replaced by next routine inspection. 

Note: staff remarked that mop hanging racks are not user friendly. Consider replacing so staff can use it properly.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. 

Dish machine was disassembled and cleaned prior to inspector arrival. When inspector arrived, machine was put back together and tested for sanitizing temperatures. After more than 10 tries, the temperature on the disc thermometer (both inspector's and facility's) reached a max surface temperature of 155. PIC Nicky called technician Auto-Chlor to service machine. PIC advised to utilize 3-part sink in the meantime to wash, rinse, and sanitize equipment. Customer dishes are all disposable. Follow-up to occur tomorrow 2/26/2021. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

Sanitizer dispenser close to empty upon inspector arrival and spray bottle used for sanitizing tables at 0ppm. CFM Colleen replaced dispenser bottle and sanitizer shows 400ppm. Violation is corrected. 

4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

Facility uses tongs to scoop servings of meat into a plastic cup to shape them for sandwiches. Cups are cleaned every day at 2PM. Facility is open 11a-9p. Discussed frequent switching out/washing of these cups (at least every 4hours) as they may grow pathogens as they sit at room temperature. PIC noted they conduct "meat checks" every 2 hours, and will adjust their SOP to include a cup change at this time as well. Violation is corrected.
